children: Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz may be higher than initial vessel-tracking data suggest, as movements made without live signals can take days to confirm, commodities-data firm Kpler says. Recent estimates have varied widely, but Kpler says much of the divergence between tracked and official figures reflects differences in methodology and timing rather than missing barrels. Its tracked Hormuz clearance has averaged 8.6 million barrels a day since mid-June, while the latest seven days remain preliminary and typically revise higher as additional vessel movements are confirmed.
